inlines.text: Use a Venn diagram of a universal set

answer.short: Both sides shade only the region outside both $A$ and $B$, inside $U$.
answer.worked: $\overline{A\cup B}$ shades everything outside both circles. $\overline A\cap\overline B$ retains the region outside $A$ and outside $B$. The shaded regions coincide.

spec.description: Paired identical two-set diagrams, exterior shaded, with each side of the identity beneath its diagram.
spec.mathematics: Complement of union equals intersection of complements.

answer.short: Both sides shade all of $U$ except the overlap $A\cap B$.
answer.worked: $\overline{A\cap B}$ leaves only the common lens unshaded. $\overline A\cup\overline B$ includes every region outside at least one circle, also leaving only the common lens unshaded.

spec.description: Paired diagrams shaded everywhere except the common lens.
spec.mathematics: Complement of intersection equals union of complements.
